sections.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: Why are the early years called the formative years?
questions.answer: Because the foundation for physical, cognitive, socio-emotional and language development is laid in this period.

questions.q: How much of brain development is complete by the age of six?
Name any two factors that lead to developmental delays.
questions.answer: Any two: an unhealthy home or school environment, too little stimulation, inadequate nutrition, poor health care.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: ECCE is an ________ programme with several components.
Name any two components of ECCE.
questions.answer: Any two: health, nutrition and hygiene; care and protection; early stimulation; early learning.

questions.q: How does quality ECCE help a child later in school?
questions.answer: The child gains age-appropriate knowledge and skills and adjusts better to the formal school environment.

sections.passage: Early childhood refers to the early years of life from birth to six years. These years are called the formative years as the foundation for physical, cognitive, socio-emotional and language development is laid during this period. Research in neuroscience shows that by the time a child is six years old, 90% of brain development has taken place. Lack of a healthy home and school environment, too little stimulation, inadequate nutrition and poor health care are common factors that lead to developmental delays. ECCE is an integrated programme whose components — health, nutrition and hygiene; care and protection; early stimulation; and early learning — together contribute to the development and wellbeing of children. Quality ECCE helps children acquire age-appropriate knowledge and skills and adjust better in a formal school environment.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What were the contributions of Gijubhai Badheka and Tarabai Modak to preschool education in India?
questions.answer: Gijubhai Badheka believed good education is vital for proper development and founded Bal Mandir, a preschool, in Bhavnagar, Gujarat in 1920. Tarabai Modak founded the Nutan Bal Shikshan Sangh in Bombay (Mumbai) in 1926, where children of different backgrounds learnt through activities and real-life experiences.

questions.q: What are gross motor skills? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Gross motor skills involve the large muscles and control big body movements. Examples: crawling, standing, walking, climbing, running, jumping.
questions.note: April 2023 asked for a one-sentence explanation of gross motor development. Lesson 7.

questions.q: Write two examples each of gross motor and fine motor skills developed by children aged three to six years.
questions.answer: Gross motor: running, jumping, throwing and kicking; catching a bounced ball; pedalling a tricycle; hopping on one foot. Fine motor: drawing a circle or square; cutting with blunt scissors; buttoning clothes; tying shoelaces; using a spoon and fork.
questions.note: October 2024 asked for examples of gross motor skills only. Lesson 9.

questions.q: What care and protection should an ECCE worker take for children in the centre?
questions.answer: Keep the centre physically safe and supervise children all the time; ensure hygiene, clean water and safe food; follow immunisation and health check-ups; respond warmly to children's needs and protect them from stress, rough handling and neglect so they feel emotionally secure.

questions.q: Mention any four common activities for all-round development.
questions.answer: Any four: free and structured conversation, storytelling and story-making, dramatisation, rhymes and songs, music and movement, sand play, water play, puppet play, circle time, free indoor play with puzzles, beads and blocks, outdoor play, nature walks, field trips.

questions.q: What activities can a teacher do to promote writing readiness?
questions.answer: Activities for eye-hand coordination and small muscles: clay modelling, colouring within an enclosed space, drawing on a slate or the floor, tracing, copying forms, joining dots, drawing zig-zag and straight lines, tearing and pasting. Formal writing should come only when children are ready.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: How does India's multi-cultural society contribute to diverse social environments for children?
questions.answer: India is a pluralistic society where people of different religions, languages, castes, tribes and economic backgrounds live together, across varied regions (Himalayas, plains, deserts, coasts). These differences in beliefs, resources, food, dress and customs give children very different experiences of childhood; some groups are disadvantaged by caste discrimination, poverty or remoteness.

or.q: What factors contribute to the poor health and living conditions of children in India?
or.answer: Uneven distribution of economic resources, lack of access and awareness lead to ill health, high-density living and unhygienic conditions. Other causes are malnutrition (stunting, wasting), infection and lack of sanitation and clean water, poor maternal health and early marriage, and gender bias against girls in health care and nutrition.

questions.q: Discuss any three characteristics of the newborn with examples.
questions.answer: Umbilical cord: bluish-white; the stub left after cutting dries and falls off within three weeks, becoming the belly button. Skin: wet and coated with white vernix caseosa (an antibacterial barrier), greyish-blue until breathing starts. Hair: fine body hair called lanugo on the back, shoulders and face, disappearing within weeks. Others: a large head for the body, weight of 2.5–3.5 kg, waking every two to three hours, and inborn reflexes.

or.q: Discuss any three milestones of language development of 2–3-year-old children.
or.answer: Any three: has a word for almost everything; uses two- or three-word phrases to talk about and ask for things; is understood by family and friends; names objects to ask for them; answers routine questions ('What is your name?'); follows two-step directions ('Find your shoes and get your dress'); begins to use plurals, prepositions ('in the jar'), possessives ('mine'), adjectives and '-ed' for the past tense; enjoys simple stories, songs and rhymes.

questions.q: What factors should be considered in designing an environment conducive to play and early learning?
questions.answer: Ease of supervision and guidance; attention to safety; maximum space for free movement; children's interests; needs of the group and of each child; special activities placed where they are readily available; similar activities kept together; furniture and shelves of suitable size and height. Materials should be attractive and within children's reach, and adults should be present to interact.

questions.q: What are the different types of records maintained in an ECCE centre?
questions.answer: Children's records (profile/cumulative record, attendance register, checklists, portfolio, progress reports, observations); staff records (personal details, qualifications, job description, salary, training, attendance); stock records (equipment, furniture, learning materials); financial records (cash book, ledger, balance sheet, fees, receipts, bank records); miscellaneous records (safety inspection book, menu, log books, prospectus, PTA minutes, visitor's book, photographs).

questions.q: What makes an ECCE teacher effective? Describe three qualities with examples from the classroom.
questions.answer: Any three, e.g.: Loving and caring — unconditional love builds trust and belonging and helps socio-emotional development. Active and empathetic listener — understands children's thoughts and feelings and solves behaviour problems. Patient and persistent — repeats and supports without anger. Flexible and adjusting — works with limited resources and diverse needs. Creative and innovative — nurtures curiosity and new ideas. Effective communicator — clear, simple language and good rapport with parents. Well trained and a lifelong learner.
questions.note: October 2021 asked: what are the qualities of an effective ECCE teacher? Lesson 17.

questions.q: How do diverse groups in a school environment provide opportunities for mutual learning?
questions.answer: Each child brings experiences of different customs, festivals, food, languages and ways of life. Sharing these — food days, festival discussions, stories and songs in different languages — lets children learn from one another, explore and celebrate in a safe, nurturing environment, appreciate differences, develop respect and empathy, and learn that all are equal.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: List the major policies and plans related to ECCE in India and explain any three.
questions.answer: Policies and plans: NPE 1986; National Nutrition Policy 1993; NPC 1974/2013; National ECCE Policy 2013; National Health Mission 2013; India Newborn Action Plan 2014; SDG 4.2; NPAC 2016; National Health Policy 2017; POSHAN Abhiyan 2018. (1) NPE 1986: ECCE strengthens primary education; child-centred, play-based; no formal 3Rs; community involvement. (2) National ECCE Policy 2013: universal access to quality ECCE for under-sixes; vision of holistic development and active learning capacity through free, universal, inclusive, equitable, joyful and contextualised opportunities; includes the Curriculum Framework and Quality Standards. (3) NPAC 2016: 'Last Child First' — priority to the most vulnerable; rights to survival, dignity, health, nutrition, education, development, protection and participation; framework for state plans.

questions.q: What is early intervention? Describe its advantages and the characteristics of quality interventions.
questions.answer: Early intervention means doing things as early as possible to work on a child's developmental, health and support needs, usually from birth to five, through services such as screening, speech, physical and occupational therapy, psychological, medical and nutrition services, home visits and social work. Advantages: better developmental, social and educational gains; less isolation, stress and frustration for families; fewer behaviour problems through positive strategies; children grow into productive, independent adults; lower future costs of special education and health care. Quality interventions are: family-centred — family works alongside professionals, flexible setting, support and guidance; developmentally appropriate — designed for the disability, trained staff, individual plans reviewed regularly, progress tracked; child-focused — practise skills in different settings, mix with peers; supportive and structured — a comfortable, well-organised, regular and predictable environment.
